questions.stem: Consider the following statements about INFLATION INDICES in India. 1. CPI-Combined is compiled and released by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI. 2. CPI-IW (Industrial Workers) is released by the Labour Bureau and anchors Dearness Allowance. 3. WPI current series has base year 2011-12. 4. The RBI's flexible inflation target of 4 % ±2 is anchored on CPI-Combined. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. CPI-Combined — NSO/MoSPI. CPI-IW — Labour Bureau (base 2016 = 100). WPI current base 2011-12 (revised from 2004-05; proposal under discussion to shift to 2017-18 or 2022-23). The RBI's Monetary Policy Framework Agreement 2015 and subsequent statutory framework under RBI Act (Section 45ZA) set a CPI-Combined target of 4 % with a ±2 % tolerance band.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): When the RBI raises the REPO RATE, banks typically raise their lending rates, cooling aggregate demand. REASON (R): A higher repo rate makes it costlier for banks to borrow overnight from the RBI, so they pass the higher cost through to customers.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false

questions.explanation: Repo rate = rate at which RBI lends to banks against government securities (very short-term, mainly overnight). When the repo rises, banks' marginal cost of funds rises, and under the MCLR (and now EBLR for retail loans) regime, lending rates tend to follow. Higher borrowing cost → less credit-fuelled demand → cooling effect on inflation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most characteristic of STAGFLATION?

options.option_text: Low growth + low unemployment + low inflation
Low / stagnant growth + high unemployment + high inflation

questions.explanation: Stagflation = stagnation + inflation. Its hallmark is simultaneous high unemployment (or low growth) AND high inflation — something the original Phillips curve couldn't explain. Classic case: 1970s OECD after oil shocks. Supply-side shocks (like a spike in crude) are a common trigger.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE (MPC). 1. It has six members: three from the RBI and three external members appointed by the Central Government. 2. The MPC meets at least four times in a financial year. 3. Decisions are taken by majority, with the RBI Governor having a casting vote in case of a tie. 4. The MPC was constituted under the RBI Act, 1934 as amended in 2016. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Composition: Governor (Chair) + Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy + one RBI officer + three external members (academics/experts, 4-year terms, non-renewable). MPC meets at least 4 times a year (in practice every 2 months). Casting vote with Governor on tie. Amendment to RBI Act in 2016 (Finance Act 2016) inserted Chapter IIIF (Sections 45Z–45ZO).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a quantitative tool of monetary policy in India?
questions.explanation: Moral suasion is a QUALITATIVE (selective) tool — the RBI persuades banks to act in certain ways without formal mandate. Quantitative tools are the levers that directly affect the overall volume of credit: CRR, SLR, repo/reverse repo, OMO, MSF, Bank Rate. Other qualitative tools: margin requirements, credit rationing, direct action.

questions.stem: If the CPI-Combined was 150 in March 2025 and 156 in March 2026 (base 2012 = 100), the year-on-year CPI inflation in March 2026 is closest to:
questions.explanation: YoY inflation = (new − old)/old × 100 = (156 − 150)/150 × 100 = 6/150 × 100 = 4.0 %. The trap is using (156 − 150)/100 = 6 % (wrong base). Always divide by the EARLIER index, not the index-base of 100.

questions.stem: Using the Fisher relation (real rate ≈ nominal − inflation), in which case does the NOMINAL rate UNDERSTATE the real return?

options.option_text: Inflation equals the nominal rate exactly

questions.explanation: Real = nominal − π. If π < 0 (deflation), real > nominal → nominal UNDERSTATES the real return. If π > 0 (typical inflation), real < nominal → nominal OVERSTATES the real return. If π = 0, real = nominal exactly.
